# General tactics

- Begin with a shared objective for the round, then give each creature a distinct job that supports it.
- Favor actions that change the encounter now over activity that consumes a turn without advancing the objective.
- Concentrate effort when removing or containing one threat matters more than spreading pressure across many threats.
- Use visible terrain to shape approach, separation, and protection. Do not assume a route or line of sight that the tabletop does not show.
- Match positioning to purpose: close for contact, keep separation when distance is useful, and avoid abandoning a contested space without a reason.
- Protect a creature whose continued presence enables the rest of the group, but do not spend the whole round preserving a creature that can no longer affect the objective.
- Recheck the board after each meaningful state change; an earlier plan can become irrelevant when a combatant moves or becomes impaired.
- When uncertain, state the simplest complete intent supported by the visible tabletop and supplied rules.
